output.summary: A sync carries a node when its own diff has the same zero-context patch id against the old and new trunk. The carried change is kept, so the design and tests reviews stay current; run_tests re-runs, and review_impl re-runs through a new base input with a sync-focused card. The budget becomes a per-stage limit (default 10) on agent rounds that raise new material findings, kept in correction_runs and counted in the stage of the node that raised them. Clean-sync re-runs never count, and capability round_budget gates the change. G1039 widens G1038's single carry predicate and reads its sync record, so it must merge after G1038.

spec:
Found while dogfooding Release 1. Every sync of a goal with the integration branch marks test_design, review_tests, implement, run_tests and review_impl stale, even when the goal's own diff did not change. G1027 synced twice and ran out of its correction budget (19 of 18) mostly that way.

Owner decisions (verbatim):
- "Ok I guess, but syncing to trunk changes things semantically like you said."
- On what re-runs after a sync merge where the goal's own diff didn't change, the owner chose "Tests + code review": design and tests reviews stay valid; run_tests always re-runs, and review_impl re-runs with a card focused on what the trunk merge brought in.
- "I think we may as well get these done now, before dogfooding again"

Scope:
- A sync whose goal diff is unchanged (the goal's own changes against the new trunk equal its changes against the old trunk, apart from context) keeps design, review_design, approve_design, test_design, review_tests and implement current.
- run_tests always re-runs after a sync.
- review_impl re-runs after a sync; its card shows what the trunk brought in that touches the goal (files the goal also changes, names it uses) and asks for semantic conflicts, not a full re-review.
- A sync that changes the goal's diff (conflict resolutions, or trunk changes inside the goal's hunks) stales as today.
- Re-runs caused by a clean sync do not count against the goal's correction budget.

Budget redefinition (owner: "Ok go with the recommendation", answering "why does a goal even _need_ a correction budget?"):
- The budget's job is to catch reviews that never converge (a new material finding every round, so no single finding repeats and no dispute fires). Today it counts every correction run, and its only firing in the Release 1 run (G1027, 19 of 18) was a false positive caused by syncs and reorder resubmits.
- Redefine it as a limit on review rounds per stage that raise new material findings. Re-runs after a clean sync, resubmits that only carry findings forward, and run_tests reruns do not count.
- Default about 10 such rounds per stage (G1026's design took 7 to 8 real rounds). Reaching it asks the owner, as today, to continue, hold or cancel.
- Acceptance adds: replaying G1027 does not reach the budget; replaying G1026's design rounds counts only rounds with new material findings.

Acceptance:
- Replaying G1027's second sync (onto G1022) keeps the reviews of design and tests, re-runs run_tests, and gives review_impl a sync-focused card that names the graph26 fixture change.
- A conflicting sync stales as today.
- This PR edits docs/design/SPEC.md and DESIGN.md for every contract change it makes and adds a HISTORY §4 row.
title: A clean trunk sync keeps design and tests reviews; run_tests and a focused code review re-run
